title.narrative: Detailed engineering designs incorporating relevant hazard resilience measures are developed
Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning
Teachers with knowledge of gender-sensitive pedagogy, including identifying and referring Gender Based Violence (GBV) and Violence Against Children (VAC)
Syllabus, teachers guides, pupils’ books are developed, printed, and distributed for school years 1-6.
Targeted education facilities constructed or strengthened to improved performance levels to one or more natural hazards (including climate related impacts)
Direct beneficiaries with increased safety from new and strengthened education facilities (disaggregated by gender)
Teachers are trained to implement revised curriculum and assessments
Primary and Secondary schools using the new EMIS with up-to-date data in the system according to established guidelines.
Teachers delivering revised curricula and assessments
Primary schools recorded sex-disaggregated results from classroom assessment and large-scale assessments (Standardized Test of Achievement of Tonga) in EMIS.
A comprehensive EMIS is established, and staff are trained.
Communities, parents and students are informed about the revision of curricula and assessments
Curricula for the selected subjects and class levels are revised.
Pilot school maintenance plans developed and implemented for selected schools
School Infrastructure Maintenance Manuals are delivered and adopted by MET
Strategic School Infrastructure Management and Development Plan developed
Immediate response mechanism established and ready to provide access to financial resources in case of an eligible climate-related crisis or emergency
WASH facilities delivered under the project include gender and disability accommodating design
Beneficiaries are satisfied with the quality of new or upgraded education facilities
Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning - Female
